definition: A training technique that uses lower-precision numerical formats (like 16-bit floating point) for most computations while retaining higher precision where needed, to speed up training and reduce memory use.
details: Mixed precision training significantly reduces memory footprint and increases training throughput on modern hardware, with minimal impact on model accuracy when implemented carefully.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Mixed Precision Training.
